h: Baggies, trams and Black Country heritage
p: West Bromwich is right in the thick of the Black Country, which means a bouncy session can easily be paired with some of the region's best heritage days out. If you're booking for a party or a big family group, try to get everyone there at the same time so nobody misses the safety briefing. Smaller children often do best on the gentler sections first, building up to the big slides once they've found their feet.

Football fans will know the town as home to West Bromwich Albion, who play at The Hawthorns. Even on a non-match day it's a familiar landmark, and the area has a strong local pride you'll notice as soon as you arrive. Tucked away in the town, Oak House is a striking timber-framed house from the 1600s with period rooms and gardens, a surprising slice of history in a busy town.

For a full day, the Black Country Living Museum in Dudley is a short drive away, with recreated streets, old shops, a fairground and canal boat trips into limestone caverns. Fans of Peaky Blinders may recognise some of it from the screen. Dudley Zoo and Castle shares a hillside next door, combining animals with medieval ruins. Closer to home, Sandwell Park Farm in Sandwell Valley has animals and a walled garden for a gentle wander. The West Midlands Metro tram runs through West Bromwich, linking it to Birmingham city centre and Wolverhampton, which makes car-free days out pretty easy.
